method: Each page was fetched on the check date and the statements the article relies on were located in the page text. Findings are paraphrased here; the pages themselves are the source. Nothing in the article is a quotation from these pages. The rules in the article's code block are our own, built on the engine's break_of_structure rules.

definition_sources.name: LuxAlgo library: Change of Character (CHoCH)
what_it_says: A change of character is the first structural break against the prevailing trend; a break of structure is its with-trend counterpart.

Vocabulary is not standardized: many traders use CHoCH and market structure shift interchangeably; others reserve MSS for a counter-trend break with displacement right after a liquidity sweep. Neither usage is official.
Which swing: the strictest common reading uses the higher low that produced the trend's final high; a looser one accepts any recent higher low, internal ones included, with more false alarms.
A body close beyond the level, ideally with displacement, is the usual filter.
Describes a lone change of character as failure-prone and as evidence, not confirmation.
definition_sources.note: https://www.luxalgo.com/library/concept/market-structure-shift/ answers HTTP 308 with a redirect to the change-of-character page (checked with curl on 2026-11-22 local time).

definition_sources.name: TMGM academy: Market Structure Shift
what_it_says: A market structure shift is a change in price structure: price breaks a meaningful swing point against the existing trend.
Break of structure generally indicates continuation; the MSS / CHoCH distinction is less consistent across frameworks and some traders use the terms interchangeably.
A structural break alone can meet a broad definition; a stricter ICT-style approach adds displacement and context. A sweep is not universally required.
A body close offers clearer confirmation than a wick-only break.
No universally accepted mechanical definition of a valid MSS exists; pivot-based indicators confirm swings late, which makes historical signals look clearer than live ones.

definition_sources.name: ATAS blog: Understanding Market Structure and Market Structure Shift (MSS)
what_it_says: MSS: price breaks a key swing high or low against the prevailing trend.
CHoCH is described as an early warning; MSS as stronger evidence, often accompanied by a fast, impulsive move.
Liquidity is context, not a requirement; the labels should not be read mechanically.
Does not say whether a candle close is needed.

definition_sources.name: LiteFinance: ICT Market Structure Shift
what_it_says: CHoCH: a break of a significant higher low or lower high; needs neither a liquidity sweep nor displacement.
MSS: stricter criteria, typically a liquidity sweep followed by a decisive move; displacement is presented as a key feature.
A candle must close beyond the level; a wick alone is not enough.
On the sweep the page is not consistent: one section says it is not always required, another says to look for one before confirming.
Attributes the ICT methodology to Michael Huddleston; cites no specific lecture or year.

definition_sources.name: Backtrex blog: Market Structure Shift vs CHoCH
what_it_says: MSS needs three things: a prior liquidity sweep, an impulsive displacement candle that leaves a fair value gap, and a candle close beyond the last major swing.
CHoCH: the first break of a swing against the dominant trend, with no displacement and no sweep required.
BOS: a break in the direction of the trend.
Refers to an official ICT definition and to Michael Huddleston without citing a lecture, a course or a date.
Presents no backtest results of its own.

definition_sources.name: TradingView: Smart Money Concepts (SMC) [LuxAlgo], open-source script
what_it_says: Labels BOS and CHoCH on internal and swing structure. The description does not define the difference between the two labels.
definition_sources.not_read: The Pine Script source was not visible in the fetched page, so the article says nothing about how that script decides between the labels and does not cite it.

origin.conclusion: No dated, written primary source for 'market structure shift' or 'change of character' was found. Two of the five pages credit the method to Michael Huddleston; none cites a lecture or a date. The article attributes no wording to him.
